findings.explanation: The root links its analysis inputs and software, but recursively following the declared raw-gaze module reaches an absolute lab source URL. Partial is defensible for the expressly recursive boundary. This is a nested source-regeneration defect, not proof that the published gaze inputs required by the paper are missing.

The three root datasets/components have versioned Git links; the phase2 child names a machine-local source. That concrete structural defect supports partial independently of remote reachability. The assessment correctly separates it from the unperformed payload retrieval check.

The modern analysis route includes REMoDNaV through a pinned component and declares its scientific and PDF tools in Dockerfile plus package metadata. The native equivalent-evidence rule accepts package declarations; unpinned apt versions are not evidence of software exclusion.

The frozen Git tree and histories contain manuscript, analysis source, configuration and gitlinks. Omitted captured files do not negate their original version control. The mapping-questioned flag appropriately prevents checkout cleanliness from replacing this criterion.

The manifest inventory identifies annex symlink keys for the large layer and gaze files, and the phase2 README explains the metadata/payload split. This establishes the tracking mechanism without asserting that absent bytes were downloaded.

The 2023 run explicitly records container/image and img/results_def.tex, and its parent tree identifies the saved image. In contrast, the upstream label run records a shell action and data inputs but no exact environment. The root histogram function consumes those labels, so this is a relevant partial lineage gap.

README supplies install links, clone instructions and concrete numerical/PDF commands. Its original and container routes are explicitly distinguished, which satisfies the disclosure exception rather than triggering a conflict penalty.

The named results-containerized tag resolves in the frozen Git objects to the cited completed run; Docker-Makefile implements the results target and delegates main.pdf. These form identifiable starting points, without requiring this reviewer to execute them.

The current script constructs inputs and output paths relative to the root. The linked labels submission scripts contain a fixed personal initial directory and Python executable. Partial is therefore grounded in actual scripts; container-internal cleanup paths should not be treated as host leakage.

For the declared modern replay route, the imported scientific packages are represented by Dockerfile/package declarations, and Makefile rendering tools are included. DataLad retrieval inside the script is optional because the run record provisions its inputs first. This supports the stated modern-route judgment, not a claim that the historical Condor route has a complete environment.

README provides tested platforms and Docker compatibility, and registration describes mount/HOME behavior. The inspected adapter explicitly assumes Docker on PATH with non-root access, while the linked legacy scripts assume a lab directory and Python 2.7. These concrete remaining assumptions justify partial.

README and Dockerfile collectively provide a clear modern-route host/tool dependency list. This criterion does not require every detail of host configuration to be repeated in README; the separate permission/configuration gap remains correctly identified under must/011.

The recipe, registration and install_requires declaration are tracked at the specified root/component revisions. Environment completeness and identity are distinct questions, so those limitations do not erase this version-control property.

The assessment narrows an environment-update process to a later package-dependency edit. The 2025 record instead gives an executed command that loads the existing archived image with Docker v26 and replaces its representation with OCI; the Git change updates the manifest/index and content paths, and README explains the Docker compatibility change. This is maintenance of an existing environment after an external dependency changed, not initial introduction. Lack of a scientific rerun is irrelevant to this update-process item.
findings.suggested_correction: Credit the documented and tracked 2025 compatibility update as an instance and revise to met, or explicitly justify from the native instrument why container-format/host-runtime compatibility updates are excluded. Apply the same conclusion to both duplicated criteria.

findings.explanation: The saved image carries config and layer identities, and the adapter computes the image ID from the saved configuration before invoking Docker. RepoTags latest is not the runtime selector. This supports an exact-environment attempt even though rebuilding the mutable apt/base recipe need not reproduce it.
findings.suggested_correction: For the adapter citation, retain the frozen source SHA-256 or use a commit-addressed upstream URL; the release-tag URL alone is not content-immutable.

findings.explanation: The native protocol requires independent recipient retrieval, which this inspection-only cohort prohibits. Source URLs, historical execution and annex location metadata cannot replace that check. Not-checked is justified; intentional capture omissions are not retrieval failures.

README gives an obtain-and-run sequence and the named registration exists. The container path and Make targets supply the mechanism behind the documentation; a new successful replay is not required for the documentation property itself.
The connected source and data repositories use Git identities, with DataLad/git-annex augmenting the same structure for payloads. No incompatible second component-versioning system is evidenced.

The history establishes individual executions, not a regular test cadence for the study instructions. The linked Travis definition tests the software package rather than root numerical/PDF reproduction. Not-checked avoids interpreting missing proof as an established absence of testing.

The root separates raw gaze, precomputed labels, reusable software, study code and container definition. Numerical macros and figure outputs are identifiable separately from those inputs. These concrete boundaries support modular separation.

The completed 2023 record has exit 0 and explicit result outputs. The matching registered adapter starts a new Docker container with --rm, supplying equivalent completed-run evidence under this instrument. This is historical evidence of fresh-container testing, not an observed 2026 rerun or independent scientific validation.

The registered modern execution starts a Docker container per call, removes it on exit and uses a temporary HOME under the mount. A persistent results mount does not make the computational environment persistent. The upstream host-Python label-generation record is a separate historical route.

Initial build, numerical execution and subsequent OCI conversion are discrete successful events. They do not demonstrate regular reconstitution testing of the exact results environment. The software Travis recipe also does not supply that evidence, so not-checked is warranted.

Both the original saved-image build record and later conversion show environment artifacts archived under container/image, with content-addressed annex entries. This is evidence of archival structure and historical preservation, distinct from current public retrieval.

The assessment narrows an environment-update process to a later package-dependency edit. The 2025 record instead gives an executed command that loads the existing archived image with Docker v26 and replaces its representation with OCI; the Git change updates the manifest/index and content paths, and README explains the Docker compatibility change. This is maintenance of an existing environment after an external dependency changed, not initial introduction. Lack of a scientific rerun is irrelevant to this update-process item.

findings.explanation: The frozen material identifies no computational component with an explicit access restriction; phase2 expressly advertises unrestricted access. A lab-local URL is a portability defect, not evidence of a restriction policy. Empty-subject not-applicable is therefore a reasonable declared-scope judgment.

Independent repositories are linked as components, including nested annotation data. The lab-source link is machine-specific, preventing a fully satisfactory recursive linking judgment. Ordinary Python dependencies are correctly not counted as separate project modules.

Root documentation explains the product and execution but does not explain the component relationships in detail. The labels README directs readers to Condor submission files while the recorded action uses compute_all.sh. Partial captures the incomplete navigation/recombination account without claiming no documentation exists.

Root and label modules independently pin their software and data revisions. Updating an upstream repository therefore does not automatically mutate an existing composed snapshot. Met is defensible for structural independence; it does not demonstrate compatibility of an arbitrary selected upgrade.

Gitlinks compose source/data revisions, and the run explicitly binds input module paths to the registered archived environment. These are executable composition mechanisms rather than an informal collection of unrelated URLs.

README provides DataLad navigation/replay entry points, .gitmodules identifies named component paths, and the run record identifies the consumed input branches. The item permits tooling as well as prose, so incomplete conceptual documentation under may/002 need not force this item to partial.

limitations: Inspection only: no network access, workflow execution, container build, payload acquisition or independent recipient retrieval. Scientific reproducibility and present-day access remain untested.

Frozen manifest SHA-256 e3c6253bced7d959cd59873c3d49d166bf5793906bcdf65e49e265076d215499 was verified, as were all 260 downloaded source-file hashes. Git reads used GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1. Several diff/stat reads could not access omitted blobs; retained histories, commit objects, tree entries and downloaded sources were used instead.
The external adapter was inspected through the root README tool/version and container-registration discovery path. Its frozen SHA-256 is cited because a version-tag URL alone is not immutable.

The native validator and checklist pin checks passed, but findings were independently checked against sources. The input contains all 31 IDs: 17 MUST, 9 SHOULD and 5 MAY, with no aggregate score or denominator field. No numeric review score is assigned.

Only the anonymized native JSON was reviewed; other assessment artifacts and peer reviews were not consulted. Original probe receipts were not available within the assigned input, so probe-override history itself was not independently reconstructed.

Agreement is not human approval. The disagreement about the duplicated update-process item concerns whether an executed compatibility conversion counts as environment maintenance; it does not claim that scientific results were rerun in 2025.
